tools.name: Zendesk
tools.desc: All-in-one customer service platform for businesses of all sizes
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
Requires internet connection, unusable offline
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Zendesk homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: Zendesk is an all-in-one customer service platform designed for businesses of all sizes. It offers a comprehensive suite of tools to streamline customer support operations, including ticketing, live chat, and self-service portals. Key features include a customizable interface, advanced reporting capabilities, and seamless integration with other business applications. It is suitable for companies looking to improve customer satisfaction and enhance their support team's efficiency. Zendesk is known for its scalability, allowing businesses to grow and adapt to changing customer needs. However, some users may find the pricing structure to be complex, and the platform can be overwhelming for small businesses with limited resources.
